thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High p99 latency detected for hosted-inference / us-west1 across streaming endpoints. p99 spike above SLO (target 1s). Automated paging threshold crossed at 2024-11-03T14:05:00Z :warning:
alex chen: oncall here, ack. seeing alerts on dashboards too. p95 ~ 380ms, p99 ~ 3.2s on streaming-io. Any deploys in last 3 hours?
maya singh: I pushed a kernel/compilepath rollout to tf-serving pool at 11:30 UTC — enabled TRT8 + FLASH_ATTENTION on the new compile path. It was gated by canary but we ramped to 50% 2h ago.
jordan li: logs show a bunch of decode stalls and `page_fault` traces in the kernel allocator around 11:45–13:30 UTC. correlated with the rollout PID 5287.
sam perkins: customer-impact: a handful of enterprise tenants reported timeouts and elevated error rates (5xx) starting ~13:50. Support ticket IDs 12345, 12346 opened. tagging support-bot.
support-bot: Noted. Support has opened incident SEC-12345 and notified CSM for affected customers. Drafting PSAT notice.
alex chen: can we pin the serving nodes to previous kernel variant while we triage? quick mitigation: route traffic to older kernel or rollback compile flag.
maya singh: we can flip routing via runtime policy. option1: route 100% of streaming traffic to fallback model variant (no FLASH_ATTENTION) — immediate mitigation but will increase cost. option2: rollback the compile flag globally — riskier for other workloads.
rachel obrien: ops question — do we have safe-to-rollback window? deployments earlier today included quantization changes too.
devon ng: kernel allocator logs attached — excerpt:
```
E decode_host: tail latency spike
E kernel_alloc: page_fault count=789
W trt_kernel: fallback to generic conv
```
maya singh: confirmed allocator page-faults spike only on nodes with TRT8+flash. non-trt hosts stable.
tess huang: past incidents show rolling back the compile flag is quickest. we can rollback the `ENABLE_FLASH_ATTENTION` flag with `kubectl set env` on deployment config and restart pods. 2–3 minute rollout per AZ.
alex chen: do it. start gradual rollback to avoid thundering herd. route 30% traffic to fallback immediately and roll back on remaining.
jordan li: prepared commands:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/inference-runtime ENABLE_FLASH_ATTENTION=false
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/inference-runtime
```
maya singh: executing now on canary group.
deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by maya singh for inference-runtime; rollout id 347210-A.
alex chen: monitoring metrics — dashboards show p99 falling in canary after 90s. p99 -> 1.1s on canary shards.
sam perkins: support: telling affected customers about mitigation and ETA for full rollback. sending interim workaround: switch to sync endpoints or smaller sequence lengths.
rachel obrien: any downstream impact on throughput? can we keep autoscale params while we rollback?
devon ng: autoscale unaffected. memory footprints are lower on fallback, no paging observed.
tess huang: request that eng-runtime prepare a patch to make FLASH_ATTENTION opt-in by model tag to avoid automatic kernel selection for streaming workloads.
jordan li: agree, adding a guard in kernel selection: prefer `generic_conv` for streaming endpoints when seq_len > 1024 until kernel allocator fix.
alex chen: rolling out to 100% now. proceeding with `kubectl` command to full rollout.
maya singh: full rollback executed. deploy-bot: rollout id 347210-B complete. pods stable.
deploy-bot: Rollout 347210-B succeeded (10/10 pods ready) :white_check_mark:
alex chen: metrics update 3m post-rollback: p95 210ms, p99 850ms — back under SLO.
sam perkins: Support update: initial customers report errors reduced, re-opening tickets for verification. CSM notified.
rachel obrien: action items: 1) eng-runtime to revert compilepath changes and add opt-in guard (owner: maya) 2) runtime to add prevention test for paging regressions on canary (owner: jordan) 3) support to send customer comms (owner: sam).
maya singh: filing PR for opt-in guard now. will also add a canary smoke test that simulates streaming tails.
jordan li: creating follow-up incident doc and root cause: likely regression in TRT8 kernel interaction with allocator under streaming tail workloads.
alex chen: handing off to night on-call. next oncall: tess huang. leave notes + links to metrics + rollback commands in incident board.
tess huang: ack'd. will monitor overnight and escalate if p99 goes over 1s again. please ping pager if regression returns.
incident-bot: Incident auto-closed for paging-latency-after-rollout when p99 < 1s for 10m. Incident summary: temporary regression caused by TRT8+FlashAttention compilepath; mitigated by rollback of ENABLE_FLASH_ATTENTION flag and routing to fallback kernel variant. Next steps tracked in RFC #928.
alex chen: thanks team. retrospective tomorrow 1600 UTC. :coffee:
